facts.status_note: Tower taken down; the register notes a mine tramway at the site, and a Colorado list calls the site a tram house, abandoned
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (register lists the San Juan National Forest)

events.note: Registered September 18, 2009 as US 529, CO 1; nominated by Susan Epstein

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register places the site in the San Juan National Forest; the Westlookouts compilation lists it under the Montezuma National Forest. The story reports both and does not choose.

Register describes a tower site that has been taken down; the Forest Fire Lookout Association Colorado list gives the type as Tram House. The brief's kind 'ground' is not stated by any source read; the story describes the tramway and tower status only.

notes_for_editor: Very thin record: no build date, design, staffing or removal year appears in any source read. Two searches and about six pages checked; the Colorado/Utah FFLA chapter site was linked from the register but not separately fetched. The 1948 abandonment is for the Alta mining town, not the tower; it is in the story only as context and the event is not tower-specific. The register's coordinates (37.885220, -107.854060) and Wikipedia's townsite coordinates (37.88583, -107.85167) are roughly 200 m apart by our reckoning, which is why the story says 'a short distance away'. Source conflicts: forest name (San Juan vs Montezuma), type (tower vs tram house), and status wording (taken down / abandoned / removed). The ghosttowntrails.com page was not used: it covers the townsite and is a membership site. Worth a human check: a current photo or Forest Service record of the tramway and whether the lookout site is open.
